title: Keyboard Manager: Unable to select specific app for remapping shortcut

judgment.rationale: A commenter supplied a concrete stateful sequence: create a Win+W mapping limited to Google Chrome, delete it, and then observe both an unresponsive target-app field and a supposedly global mapping that remains Chrome-only. The original expectation of an app suggestion list is separate and may be a UI preference, but the stale-scope behavior warrants a current-build reproduction.
evidence: The original issue reports that typing into Target app did not populate a selectable app list; it used PowerToys 0.77.0.

The 2024-04-09 comment describes a stateful failure after deleting a Win+W mapping restricted to Google Chrome: a new target-app entry appears unresponsive and a blank-target mapping still acts only in Chrome: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/31048#issuecomment-2045115206.
The 2026-07-19 comment asks why an app list is expected, but it does not answer whether the separate stale-scope sequence is fixed.
The issue is cross-referenced by #32346, which is closed as a duplicate; that closure does not itself establish that this stateful behavior was fixed.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the delete-and-recreate sequence on a current build and check both the editor field and the saved app-specific runtime mapping.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked implementation covers the reported stateful sequence. The current editor and app-specific engine paths are relevant, but the old report does not prove where stale scope is retained.

proposed_fixes.title: Clear stale target-app scope when a shortcut mapping is deleted
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: deleting and recreating an app-specific shortcut may leave the prior target-app value in the editor buffer or saved mapping state, causing the field to appear stuck and a blank target to remain scoped to Chrome. This is not confirmed.
plan: Reproduce the exact Win+W create/delete/recreate sequence in Keyboard Manager on a current build.
Inspect the target-app TextBox and remap buffer through delete, row recreation, save, and reload to identify whether stale app scope persists.
If stale state is confirmed, clear it when a row is deleted/recreated and add editor save/load tests plus an engine test proving a blank target applies globally.
Do not add an app suggestion list unless product requirements establish that behavior; it is distinct from the reported stale-scope bug.
verification: Create Win+W scoped to Google Chrome, delete it, then create a new Win+W mapping with a blank target and save.
Verify the target-app field accepts input and that the saved mapping applies both inside and outside Chrome after restarting Keyboard Manager.

confidence.rationale: The stateful symptom and trigger are documented, but the report predates current builds and does not identify whether the editor or engine retains the stale scope.

issue_context.summary: The original report expects an app picker, while a later comment documents a separate stale-scope failure after deleting and recreating a Chrome-specific shortcut.
known_information: The original report used PowerToys 0.77.0 and describes a target-app field that accepts typing but does not show a list.
A commenter reproduced a stateful sequence in 0.80.0: add Win+W scoped to Google Chrome, delete the mapping, then find that a new mapping is still Chrome-only.
The issue has two comments and no assignee.
The related issue #32346 is closed with state reason duplicate; no fix commit is linked from the selected issue.
inferences: The app list may not be an intended autocomplete behavior; the separate stale-scope outcome is still a plausible functional defect.
If the delete/recreate issue persists, the stale value could be in the UI buffer, serialization, or runtime lookup.
issue_context.analysis: The supplied sequence is concrete enough for maintainers to reproduce. A focused check of the current editor and app-specific mapping flow is more useful than repeating a request for diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Read the full live body and both comments, including the later question about app-list expectations.
Read the closed linked duplicate #32346 status.

Checked the current target-app editor control and app-specific lookup in src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorLibrary/EditShortcutsWindow.cpp and src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp; these are relevant but do not confirm a stale-state root cause.

reproduce.version_requirement: Use a current supported PowerToys build; compare with the 0.80.0 reproduction in the discussion.
prerequisites: Google Chrome installed as a test target.
A second application available to test global scope.
steps: Create a Win+W shortcut remap with Target app set to Google Chrome and save it.
Create a new Win+W mapping and leave Target app blank; also test typing a different app name in the field.
Save, restart Keyboard Manager if needed, and test Win+W in Chrome and the second application.
reproduce.expected: The recreated blank-target mapping is global, and the target-app field accepts edits without retaining the deleted Chrome scope.

actions.label: Approve focused stale-scope investigation
actions.note: The suspected stale editor/runtime state is unconfirmed and scored red.
